LM model drop (1/6 scale) test on RS soil (Red Crushed Volcanic Scoria (narrowly graded)) at relative density 0; apparatus: modified 1/6-scale LM model; six-degree-of-freedom drop test rig; loading: free drop; Total Model Weight 68.4 Lbs.; yaw 45 deg (2-2 landing), zero pitch and roll, zero angular rates; level surface (ground slope 0). Recorded: absolute footpad velocity VAP vs time; footpad heading theta vs time; footpad penetration depth vs time; strut No. 1 axial load vs time; strut No. 2 axial load vs time; strut No. 3 axial load vs time; CG vertical acceleration vs time; CG vertical velocity vs time; CG vertical displacement vs time; CG horizontal velocity vs time; CG horizontal displacement vs time; vehicle pitch velocity vs time; vehicle pitch angle vs time.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 156 of the 170 points, and 6 are still under review. They have not yet been checked by a person. The test setup is incomplete: fill depth is not reported.
:::

## Data

![footpad penetration depth and axial load, strut No. 3 and axial load, strut No. 2 and axial load, strut No. 1 against time, SI units. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-mdrop-11.png){.lightbox}

Peak footpad penetration depth 106.90 mm at 99.6 ms time, the end of the record. Axial load, strut No. 3 -106.9 N at the end. Axial load, strut No. 2 224.6 N at the end. Axial load, strut No. 1 -225 N at the end.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-mdrop-11/observations.csv) (170 points: 0 plotted symbols, 142 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1 (Fig. 5-31): footpad penetration depth in m against time in s; panel 2 (Fig. 5-32): axial load, strut No. 3 in N against time in s; panel 3 (Fig. 5-32): axial load, strut No. 2 in N against time in s; panel 4 (Fig. 5-32): axial load, strut No. 1 in N against time in s; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-mdrop-11/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on these figures (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 0.211 ms in time, 572 micrometers in footpad penetration depth (Fig. 5-31) (0.5 percent of the peak), 4.254 N in axial load, strut No. 3 (Fig. 5-32), 3.776 N in axial load, strut No. 2 (Fig. 5-32), 4.225 N in axial load, strut No. 1 (Fig. 5-32). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 156 of the 170 points; 6 are still under review (hollow in the plot) and 8 were settled against the scan. Check the digitized points against the scan: [F5-31](../figures/index.qmd#check-f5-31), [F5-32](../figures/index.qmd#check-f5-32).

**About these values.** No. 1 footpad of the 1/6-scale model, NASA Test No. 2. The depth is a computed output, not a direct measurement: the report's data reduction program took the 13 tape-recorded signals every 1/1000 s and calculated the footpad's penetration by numerical integration (AM-68-1 Vol. I, Section 5.5.2, printed 5-41, PDF 321). Axial load of the strut, tension positive and compression negative, as the panel's printed labels give it (the axis title names the sense of the trace's main excursion); a trace beyond the panel's 0 line changes sense. On Fig. 5-32, past 0.09 s the time is extrapolated: the 0.10 s line is too faint on the scan to anchor, and the three strut traces end at about 0.103 s in both readings. On the Strut No. 2 panel the top load label is printed -60; the panel's own sequence (0, +20, +40) and the (Tension) title make it +60, and both readings anchor that line at +60 lbf. Where the scan has no ink the line is left open: a break in the drawn line at about 0.0089 to 0.0091 s, about 4 px of the page with no ink; a break in the drawn line at about 0.0261 to 0.0263 s, about 4 px of the page with no ink.
